title: The sharp constant of the absolute dyadic triangular Hilbert sum is at least 3
description:
Let Λ(F0,F1,F2) = Σk ΣI ∈ Ak |LI| be the sum of absolute local contributions of the dyadic triangular Hilbert form, the stronger quantity bounded in the preprint An L3 bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form (OpenAI, October 2026, github.com/openai/math), which proves Λ ≤ 40 Πv ||Fv||3. Let C* be the best constant in that estimate. We prove C* ≥ 3. The bound concerns the absolute sum only: on our witnesses the signed per-scale form is much smaller, so nothing is claimed for it.

The proof is elementary: for inputs constant on dyadic squares the form is a finite sum of integer traces, and an exact product rule describes how it transforms under Kronecker (tensor) products of inputs: R(f ⊗ g) = H(g) + |T(g)| R(f) for sign inputs. Tensor powers of one explicit 4×4 sign pattern with (H, T) = (3/2, 1/2) have ratio exactly 3 − 21−r. All values are exact rationals computed by two independent implementations (three for the first value beyond 5/2). We also prove that the sharp constant at resolution 1 is exactly 1 and that each dyadic level contributes at most Πv ||Fv||3.

We conjecture C* = 3, in the sharper tensor-closed form H(F) + 3|T(F)| ≤ 3 Πv ||Fv||3, saturated on the whole tensor family. Exhaustive search at resolution 1 and exact hill-climbs at resolutions 2–4 found no violation. The gap 3 ≤ C* ≤ 40 remains open. Nothing here is machine-checked in a proof assistant, and no person has refereed the manuscript before this preprint.

AI use: the computations, the search for the seed, the product rule and the manuscript were produced by Claude agents (Anthropic) in Claude Code under a workflow designed and launched by the author (preregistration committed before each confirmatory run, positive and negative controls, exact arithmetic, adversarial model verification). The author chose the problem and the rules.
notes: Code and exact results: github.com/xaviercallens/AutoevolveAI, branch worktree-openai-math-discovery, directory papers/dyadic_triangular_hilbert and scripts/openai_math/hypotheses/tensor (commit recorded inside the PDF). The archive bundles the paper source, the scripts, every JSON result and the sign-pattern witnesses (.npz) with a sha256 manifest.
